brief.headline: Push for a 10–15% price cut — they keep 5.9% profit vs 3.8% for similar firms, so there's room in their margin

priceAsk.summary: Ask for a 10–15% price reduction on rigid plastic packaging
priceAsk.target: Aim for ₹0.65–0.80/pc on items like the 28mm PP cap (market typical is ₹0.85–0.95/pc; modest headroom exists at higher volume)
priceAsk.basis: They keep 5.9% profit vs 3.8% for similar firms — that extra margin is room to cut price. Market research shows ₹0.55–1.20/pc ask band with typical ₹0.85–0.95/pc; verdict is 'MARKET-FAIR; modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume / looser spec'

paymentTermAsk.summary: Offer to pay in 15 days instead of 30 days in exchange for a price cut equal to their borrowing cost (about 12%)
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Paying 15 days faster frees up ₹22.57 L of our cash, but it's worth roughly 12.19% to them (their borrowing rate) — so trade that for a matching price cut

brief.financialLeverage: Chemco is healthy — CRISIL A+ rating, keeps 5.9% profit, and generates ₹118.43 Cr free cash. But their cash is stuck for 104d vs 79d for similar firms, so they need cash flow. We're tiny to them — ₹5.49 Cr is 0.59% of their ₹937.60 Cr revenue — so we can't threaten to walk away alone. Instead, dangle faster payment (worth 12.19% to them) and hint at volume growth (they're growing 22.1%/yr) to justify a serious price cut. Their high profit margin (5.9% vs 3.8%) means they can afford it.

evidence.point: They keep more profit than similar firms
Their cash is stuck longer than most
Strong credit rating — low risk of trouble
We are a small customer to them
evidence.figure: ₹5.49 Cr is 0.59% of their ₹937.60 Cr revenue

evidence.point: Market ask for 28mm PP cap shows room at volume
evidence.figure: ₹0.55–1.20/pc band, typical ₹0.85–0.95/pc, verdict: modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter (₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health B 65/100) — does pharma bottles, caps, preforms; top second-source candidate

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader (₹946.50 Cr revenue, health B 73/100) — makes pails, containers, pharma packaging; strong, profitable alternate

risks: We're only 0.59% of their revenue — too small to lean on volume alone; must sweeten with faster payment or commit to growth
Their Altman Z-score is 2.17 (grey zone) — healthy but not bulletproof; don't squeeze so hard you push them into trouble; focus on win-win (faster payment for price cut)
Market verdict says 'modest headroom' at higher volume — we need to commit meaningful volume or looser spec to justify the low end of the price band (₹0.65–0.80/pc)
They pay their own suppliers in 49d vs 37d for peers — already stretching terms upstream, so pushing them to give us longer payment terms may hit resistance
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to talk about aligning our price to the market — you're keeping 5.9% profit vs 3.8% for similar firms, and we're seeing caps at ₹0.65–0.80 at volume — so let's find a number that works for both of us, especially if we can pay you faster.
